Garmin was hit in July. The infection chain is described as starting with SocGholish fake browser updates and Cobalt Strike. Attacks involve lateral movement, encryption of files and network backups, and deletion of shadow copies. Several attributions…

e53bdd6305ffdc56960a6d31e8064bc5dc189214.summary: Proofpoint reports on TA505's September to October 2019 email campaigns, which delivered the Get2 downloader and then the SDBbot remote access trojan. Get2 was seen downloading FlawedGrace, FlawedAmmyy, Snatch and SDBbot. Campaigns targeted financial institutions and other sectors, with a recent focus on Greece, Germany and Georgia. SDBbot uses application shimming, registry Run keys or image file execution options for persistence, and offers remote shell, screen recording, remote desktop and port forwarding.

e5f00b962f311586280d3781653203e7de381979.summary: A February 2022 Linux security research blog post demonstrating how data in a running process's memory can be changed while the user sees no visible difference. It uses a text editor as the demo target. It names no threat actor, campaign, malware family, CVE or victim. The author presents the technique as an option after gaining low-privilege SSH access, and says it could disable security controls without leaving forensic artifacts.

dates.what: Blog post published, covering runtime process memory modification on Linux
